candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest classified this binary as malware with probability 1.0000, and all 20 top n-grams push toward cryptojacking (SHAP +0.0054 to +0.0096). No counter-evidence appears in the list. Several n-grams point to compute-heavy, hash-like code. Rotate instructions are ADD ROR (freq 0.002240, SHAP +0.009601, the top feature), MOV ROL (0.002495, +0.006616), ROL MOVZX (+0.005764) and ROL AND (+0.005583). Rotate-and-add mixing is typical of hashing and cipher round functions. Packed SIMD operations make up a second cluster: PXOR MOVAPS (+0.007799), MOVDQA MOVAPS (+0.007830), PXOR MOVUPS (+0.006444), PXOR PXOR (+0.005603), PXOR MOVDQA (+0.005523) and PAND PXOR (+0.006948). These indicate vectorized bitwise and XOR state manipulation over 128-bit blocks, which is consistent with mining-style hashing kernels. These patterns are also frequent, at roughly 0.001 for the PXOR/MOVAPS family and 0.002 for the rotate family. This suggests a sustained computational loop rather than incidental use. MOVAPD DIVSD (+0.007701) is very rare (0.000002) but strongly weighted. It indicates scalar double-precision floating-point division alongside packed moves, which could fit a mixed integer and floating-point workload. The remaining n-grams (POP SUB, ADD PUSH, CALL RET, POP LEA, SUB PUSH, POP CMP, MOVZX PUSH, ADD MOVQ, POP XOR) are generic stack, prologue/epilogue and arithmetic glue. Each contributes +0.0054 to +0.0077, so they are weaker individually, but they may reflect the compiled or packed code structure the model associates with miners. The evidence does not name any functions or APIs, so this assessment rests only on instruction-level statistical signatures. Crypto-heavy but legitimate software can share rotate and SIMD patterns, which keeps confidence below certainty. Still, the model's output of 1.0, the uniform positive SHAP direction and the coherence of the rotate-plus-SIMD-XOR cluster support a high-confidence call.
